components.name: camera
components.method: MoGe prior + known-geometry PnP profiles, background rotation and stationary-object camera anchors
components.note: Refined camera excludes partial-mask depth hump, max translation2.54cm. Focal regularized1050px; monocular sensitivity retained.

components.name: objects_6d
components.method: Blender geometry, SAM3/SAM2 and physically constrained render-and-compare
components.note: Watertight Blender models with white blade holes and correct socket forms; supported and physically airborne object motion, full-scene replayIoU .8774/.8069. Hidden poses invalid;10mm carry clearance inferred, absolute depth uncertain.

components.name: hand_motion
components.method: HaWoR plus mandatory MANO optimizer owned copy, all778 vertices, anatomical opposed contact and geometry-derived separation; independent installed validators
components.note: 360valid,handmaskIoU.8514; all10required checks pass; full-surface opposed-contact and support-halfspace refits, extra table check max0.426mm. Baseline and every non-default setting retained.

reprojection.note: against your own masks: agreement with them is necessary, not sufficient (3D errors along the viewing ray are invisible here)

anatomical_contact.note: a grasp needs the thumb and an opposing finger on opposite sides of the object; single-finger pushes or palm support are legitimate but must be stated in the analysis. Low penetration does not imply contact.

penetration_hand_object.note: unsigned (lower bound) distances where the object mesh is not watertight

self_penetration.note: triangle intersections between different fingers (FCL); counts are not volumes

physics.note: free-flight intervals are given with --flight OBJ=a:b; rest intervals default to object intervals without contact

handedness_scale.note: left/right are the demonstrator's anatomical hands; a hand is never mirrored

camera_focal.note: MoGe intrinsics are a learned prior; the focal should be calibrated against known geometry (camera_calib.py pnp). A large disagreement needs its explanation in NOTES.md (which one is wrong, and why).

scene.model: Full provided Marvin Wuji MJCF, both arms/hands and original collision geometry, with a single plug, table, floor, and column.

plug.state_frame: Housing centre, +Z toward blade tips, +Y across the blade gap. Identity object/body frame.
plug.geometry: Station housing and two blade OBJ parts from given/recon. Exact specified dimensions and axes.
plug.physical_prior: The comparable charger teardown weighs 58.5 g. The video supports the housing geometry and grasp scale, with no force data. Used the operator 60 g estimate and housing-plus-blades bounding-box inertia. Contact pair assumptions are 0.40 sliding at the table, 0.80 hand material friction. The PC-glass study is a material prior and its interface differs from the station. The video shows little post-release slide but does not identify either coefficient.
plug.contact: Housing and two blades have separate convex collision meshes. Elliptic sliding and torsional contact, solref 0.012 s / damping ratio 1, solimp [0.93,0.98,0.001].

reference.method: White cycle with d2s_reference progress, object start and goal alignment and SLERP. Palm axis mapping is derived from reconstructed MANO joints. Applying a world-up yaw adjustment of 150 degrees to the wrist and its offset selects a more reachable approach heading while keeping plug start and goal constraints. The palm height is projected above -0.225 m in the retarget. These embodiment adjustments guide rewards and are not executed trajectories.

body.arm: Measured-seed DLS IK, 1 and 0.2 position/rotation weights, eight updates per 100 Hz tick, a soft home preference and approach-to-column rejection using the collision capsules. Right arm 5-degree-margin limits, 20 mm and 0.075 rad per tick sent-target caps, published jump and box checks, per-joint command rate capped at 3.1416 rad/s. Models the joint-specific delay and low-pass response and impedance relative to command velocity. Joint torques use full physical contact generalized forces with a 30 ms external-torque estimator. The parked left side has its original collision masks.
body.hand: Public geometry and deployed limits including the 1 mm glove collision margin. Finger targets have 35 ms delay and 2 Hz low pass. Internal position gains are 12x vendor kp and 3x vendor kv as a response approximation with current-limited torque. Nominal evaluation uses 0.6x joint effort, with 0.1 deg encoder noise.
body.sensor: Default d2s_sensor.PoseSensor fed at 60 Hz. 48 surface samples from the complete object mesh, visual points clipped by calibrated ego-camera geometry. Arm caps and fitted capsules for hand-link mesh occluders. Proprioception delayed by a lognormal draw quantized to the nearest 60 Hz row.

initial_conditions.object: Uniform independent x/y offsets ±10 mm and blade yaw ±10 degrees about -90 degrees, X-up on the supported face.
initial_conditions.start_check: Hold controller uses the reset palm so the entire hold check, including any ramp rows, can test a stationary hand. Candidate evaluation simulates the actual package start ramp.

body.limitations: The kinematic replay has large positional errors and brief hand–plug overlap, and uses a visualization-only aperture. It is not evidence of physical feasibility. Ramp lag at the recommended start is 32.7 mm, above the station example 18–25 mm, so the first action needs margin. No measured glove friction or plug mass from the station. Independent parity is pending for any parallel training backend.

body.text: The reconstructed approach yaw is outside the robot's reachable branch. The wrist-only retarget improves reach but still has a 44 mm median positional error and 3.7 mm maximum overlap in a kinematic replay. I am fitting an opposed pinch on the plug's width faces, then testing whether differential finger motion can rotate it about the width axis while keeping the wrist excursion close to the video. The first static fit touched both sides in some rollouts, but all grasps lost opposition at lift in the tested draw. The next test increases inward pad travel and uses gentler lift.

body.method: privileged geometry fit and contact-physics waypoint search
body.hypothesis: An opposed width-face pinch with added preload and synchronized leftward wrist travel will lift and carry the plug across randomized starts. The local baseline sometimes reached the goal but still showed late reorientation and intermittent loss of opposition.
body.observed: The demonstration keeps finger opposition during the turn. The local baseline attained 5.6 degrees from upright during opposed contact on one draw, then lost that contact before stable placement.
body.success_rule: every stage, hardware within limits, no stop
body.reason: first gate of this suite version: the baseline, now the incumbent

body.text: In r0008 the feasibility baseline lifted 32/32 and passed no turns. In seed 457221813 the montage shows the plug on the table by 10.03 s, and the sampled contacts show a loss of thumb opposition by 6.183 s while it is airborne. Seed 351492938 also lost opposition during the turn, and exceeded a deployed finger limit by 0.040 rad. In local full-rate traces the initial opening stroke drives the desired turn, but the pad opens before the table takes the load. The new controller splits that stroke into active roll, maintained contact during descent, and release. I will also test a stiffer physical finger stop against the documented 0.02 rad allowance. Policy weights still start from scratch.

body.text: Dynamic CPU/Warp outcome parity passed on 128 matched full-range starts with the same fixed feasibility plan: 8/128 CPU and 11/128 GPU, zero hardware violations in both. This was a 13 s plan plus settling comparison, separate from the 60 s gates. The end-to-end PPO experiment will use the matched GPU scene, a deployable observation history and reference-progress rewards. Mid-skill curriculum resets use physically realised simulator qpos/qvel and contact phases aligned to the reconstruction. The PPO learner reads no controller actions, and no weights are initialized from feasibility rollouts. Budget the first PPO configuration 60 million active steps, with CPU checkpoint tests and continued training if the curve is still improving.

body.text: Task feasibility is proven. Begin the 60-million-active-step PPO experiment from random weights, with the matched GPU simulator, state-only curriculum reset bank, default noisy sensor, and no demonstration or controller actions in training.

Stopped the first PPO launch after the initial batch produced non-finite reward and loss values. It did not yield an evaluated policy. The training loop now detects numerical divergence in each Warp world, charges a failed episode, resets that world, and checks advantages before optimization. The CPU evaluator and criteria are unchanged. Restart from random weights.

The restarted PPO run has finite losses and active-state KL near 0.01, with early returns improving and occasional completion from late curriculum resets. Launch a second random seed with the same PPO configuration on an idle GPU to measure seed sensitivity. Select any recorded evaluation on simulator results, using the frozen task gate for every kept package.

body.text: Task baseline r0022 has valid contract logs and no hardware violations. In seed 1570346490 at 2.30 s, the fingers reach the plug, but by 10.00 s the side view shows the fingers above the plug with its housing still on the table. Test a closer pre-grasp package start as a parallel PPO experiment while the two recommended-start seeds continue. The pose held without contact or stops on all 64 development draws and maintained full reported visibility. The reward, PPO architecture, full plug start distribution and physics are the same. Budget 30 million active steps for this branch.

The alternate pre-grasp exposed a GPU ramp parity bug. Its quaternion descriptor was in the opposite hemisphere from the reset quaternion, and the GPU linear blend took the long path. Match the CPU sign choice before the blend. The corrected GPU ramp then passed 256 randomized hold starts with no stop, limit excursion, or contact, and full reported visibility at hold. Restart the branch from scratch. The first alternate-start launch produced no evaluated policy.

body.reflection: Continued the same PPO configuration. On 64 full CPU episodes, all four stages remained at zero with no hardware violations and no stops. Largest rise remained 1.9 mm and unsupported opposition was absent. Next examine preload and supported pinch quality while completing the method budget.

body.text: r0022 montage seed 1281518469 shows an early digit tap with the housing supported, followed by a rise of the hand alone. In matched dev seed 8173501, the 6.09M policy peaked at 0.32 N of opposing normal force, the 10.33M checkpoint had no opposed force in its first 6 s, and the feasible fixed motion sustained 3 to 5 N with nearly antiparallel normals. Binary simultaneous contact rewards incidental taps. A proposed acquisition reward uses the simulated minimum opposed normal component, capped at 2.5 N, and qualifies the existing acquisition bonus after three 30 Hz samples above 1.4 N. A same-rays plan check across 24 starts averaged +28.99 versus hold -0.79 and random -2.18, with 24 qualifying plan lifts and zero plan hardware violations. This is training-only reward guidance and changes no policy input or evaluation rule. The two original seeds continue their 60M step budget. The 10.33M assessment is iteration r0025.

Physical reset audit in 1323 snapshots found a curriculum defect. Resetting hand targets to measured angles unloads the contact before learning can act. After a 0.1 s hold, 167/312 turn states and 17/175 carry states retained unsupported opposition. A training-only initialization solves a friction-wrench balance from each snapshot geometry and maps it through contact Jacobians and the modeled finger servos. It uses no demonstrated or controller actions. On the same randomized starts, 312/312 turn and 138/175 carry states now retain unsupported opposition at 0.1 s, with no hardware violations or stops. Save these actuator memory states in a separate reset bank. Run a concurrent single-variable curriculum repair with the original start, reward, domain randomization and PPO settings for 60M active steps. Predict lift first through better mid-state learning and later turn. Continue the original seeds to their budgets for comparison. r0022 seed 1281518469 shows lack of sustained opposition before the hand rises.

body.reflection: The fixed pre-grasp start moved the plug farther at 3.02M steps. Across 64 deployment episodes best rise was 9.3 mm and unsupported opposition remained absent. Three hardware violations and one stop occurred. Continue the 30M budget to see whether the greater interaction becomes a stable pinch.

body.text: The r0025 actor was replayed on 16 matched dev starts for 8 s with previous targets in the history replaced by measured pose/joints. Its command integration still uses the contract previous targets. Original made positive-depth contact in 13/16 and had 1.6 mm max rise with no unsupported opposition. Masked made contact in 16/16, one episode reached 21.2 mm maximum rise with 0.183 s of unsupported opposition, and both had no stops or limit violations. This is an input-ablation diagnostic of the same learned checkpoint and is not a task-gate result. It suggests the two histories may encourage target following independent of contact. Assess target dropout or a measured-hand-relative action encoding after current budgets, alongside the observed failure to load the pinch.

Correction to r0029: 21.2 mm was the maximum rise over all masked episodes (seed 8173513, no opposition). The qualifying lift was a different episode, seed 8173529, with 12.9 mm rise and 0.183 s of unsupported opposition. Masked lift count 1/16 versus 0/16 on this short diagnostic.

body.hypothesis: Replace previous palm targets with measured pose in the same trained actor's history. Removing direct target tracking from the feature values should improve grasp acquisition and qualifying lifts. The command integration and all weights are unchanged. Fixed 60 s CPU dev lifts 6/64 vs 0/64, with one finger-limit episode; this gate tests the tradeoff on paired fresh starts.
body.observed: r0022 seed 1281518469 at 3.63 s shows middle-finger contact with the plug supported. In later montage frames the hand has risen while the plug stays on the tabletop.

body.text: A reach audit found the wrist reward itself encourages an infeasible approach. Across the fixed 64 CPU starts, the uncalibrated frame-73 waypoint has median IK error 66.08 mm and only 3/64 satisfy 10 mm and 0.05 rad. The fitted pinch geometry gives 64/64 and median error 0.31 mm with a fixed palm-frame correction. Applying that correction throughout destroys reachability late, so the proposed reward fades it out across frames 130 to 148. The blended waypoints are reachable in 64/64 at frames 73 to 140, 61/64 at frame 149 and 43/64 at frame 162, versus 3/64 to 56/64 at the early frames, 56/64 and 35/64 at the last two. The object references stay reconstructed; the pool then selects by start heading as well as position. This is a wrist reward correction prepared for after the active budgets. See experiment/media/reference_alignment.json.

r0034 rejected the palm-history ablation. Candidate had 3/32 lifts in the initial sample, 4 candidate-only lifts versus zero incumbent-only on 96 paired draws (p=0.0625), zero full success, and two paired hardware violations versus zero. I reviewed both failure montages. In seed 209181378 at 2.30 s the digits bracket the housing but by 10 s there is a visible gap; the trace reports no unsupported opposition and 10.2 mm rise. In seed 493618404 the housing tilts under the finger and stays supported, later leaving the grasp region; trace reports 60.75 s of environment contact and no airborne grip. The mask improved interaction but did not reliably sustain a pinch. An updated training-only acquisition reward also preserves the starting blade posture through the pinch so table-assisted tipping does not qualify. Benchmarked on matched physical commands, 24/24 still qualified for the reward lift; mean return +29.12 versus hold -0.79 and random -2.18. No task criteria or frozen evaluator changes. Continue the active budgets.
